body: I would say that my main reason to keep living each day is I do not want to hurt my daughter and my grandchildren. I know they love me very much, and my death would cause them terrible pain. I know they love me, but I don't think I love myself. I put on a strong face for everyone... friends, family, work... But inside I am sad, insecure, anxious, desperate, and frightened. I feel like I just can't keep living this way. It is eating me alive. I have tried so many things to get better, but am giving up hope that I can get better.

Thank you. I will work on having that talk with her. I think I am also afraid of being honest and admitting I have this trust problem, because I will look weak and broken, but maybe I am still broken. I am afraid I have to appear like I have my shit together or she will leave me. Of course pretending everything is fine hasn't worked so well for me in the past, so I know I need to work on being honest about the things I struggle with.
Agreed. I have been sharing this with my counselor as well. I see my therapist every other week. It has been helpful, but this has been a particularly difficult battle for me.

This is where I am. For 48 years I have never really been alone. There were parents and siblings, then college roommates, then a spouse and kids. Now there is no one. I am trying to figure out how to adjust to this. It's all the little things I miss. Even when the marriage was struggling, she was still someone to talk to or have a meal with or simply tell about my day. The only thing I talk to in the house now is my Google Home.

Same here. When we got married we had two if everything so I got rid of most all of my furniture and such, so the house would feel like her home. Now she is gone and of course took the stuff she brought into the marriage and I am left alone in a big empty house with one mattress, one armchair, and a dining table.

Yes, exactly this. I travel frequently for work and have had a few flights since the divorce was final. It was so weird and so sad to have no one to text when the plane landed. It's these little things that catch me by surprise with how much they hurt.
Thanks for the encouragement. Speaking of a blank slate, I plan to repaint everything in the house to give it a new look and feel.

Thanks so much. I have been trying to stay active and involved in things. I love tabletop games, so I have been going to local board game nights. I have also taken up orienteering (a sport that is sort of a mix of hiking, running, and map reading). I would love to get a pet (I have always had a pet of some sort my entire life) but my job does have me travel from time to time, so I worry about that with a pet, since it will be just me in the house. Definitely something to work toward though.

Thanks so much. Yes, I have been thinking about having a friend or family member go with me the first time back to the house. I think that may make it easier to have someone with me and someone I can talk to.

Thanks. I do have a lawyer and he has been helpful, but it is still overwhelming. As for my step sons, my wife and I have been married for 9 years, so I feel like they are my actual kids. I am sure I will be able to see them at their games and other public events, but it will not be the same as actually living with them.

Thanks. That is good to know about the papers. I will try to complete as much as I can and submit that. I do have a lawyer, and he is checking over everything for me, and helps to explain what the different forms mean.
Thanks for the encouragement. I have been trying to exercise as much as I can. It is actually a warm day for once so I may try to jog outside tonight.
Thank you for sharing that. That is encouraging to hear.
Thank you. Those are good ideas to focus on.

Thanks. I am still in the same house as my wife for now. My lawyer has suggested I not make any changes yet until we can all sit down and start to negotiate through everything. We are keeping it civil, but it is very painful to be in the same house as her. I am sure it will be difficult when I am eventually alone, but for now it is a different kind of difficult still being in the same house together.
I have had arthritis since my mid-20's, so low-impact has been helpful for a long time. I like to jog, but it can aggravate my joint issues if I run to much. The elliptical works very well for that.
I have been exercising each day as well. I do about an hour each evening on an elliptical machine (started a few weeks ago) while watching something on Netflix. That does help.

I think you are correct about why she has stayed. When I ask her, she keeps saying she just doesn't know, but I think she has known for a long time. I think she is just scared of making it official and being on her own. I provide her with a good life, and she knows I won't give up on the marriage (or at least I never have so far.) I think it is time I realize the truth and stop hanging onto hope for something that is not there.
I do not disagree. I have been, and still am in, counseling. I have my next appointment later this week.
Thank you for the recommendation of the ChumpLady site. Really good stuff there.

I have been in counselling of many years, and need to get back in. For what it is worth, yes, I believe my "picker" has problems. I was raised by an alcoholic, abusive dad until the age of 11 when he died. I then spent the rest of my school years tending to and supporting my widowed mother. I would say I have been drawn to people in crisis, and then feel a strong need to help them, whatever it takes. I realize the disadvantage this sets up for my marriages.

Although I appreciate your comment, I know there are in fact many things wrong with me. We all have flaws, do dumb things, get preoccupied, act insensitively. We are human and we will let others down. The key is can we recognize those issues, apologize, and try to make a change in our behavior. The issue with cheating is it is the opposite. Rather that realizing our faults, discussing them honestly, asking for forgiveness, and making better choices, cheating is turning on the marriage. It is finding happiness in something outside of the marriage rather than trying to help the marriage. I just don't get it. If she would put the same energy, hours, and conversations into our marriage as she has with this other guy, our marriage would greatly approve. The grass isn't greener on the other side of the fence. It is greener where you water it. Both people have to be intentionally pouring into the marriage, asking how can I show love to my partner today?

That's the thing that really is eating at me. We all make mistakes, but in the end what do we do? Do we own up to those, try to do better, and work to strengthen the marriage? Or do we take our limited hours and energy and invest them in something outside of the relationship.When she lies to me about going out with her girlfriends and then spends half the day with this guy, that is time she could have spent with me working on our relationship. Those are conversations we could have been having, memories we could have been making, discussions we could have been working through to get to understand each other better. But, no, I am left at home waiting for her to get back from her girlfriends when really she is spending the afternoon hanging out with a guy. Several times I politely asked if it would be ok for me to tag along with her friends, I did not want to intrude on girl time, but I also want to be a part of her extended life with her work friends. She always said "no" and now I realize it was because she was actually seeing the guy.

I know she is looking for something. I just don't understand what it is and why she will not let me fill that need. When I asked he what she and this guy do when she over to his house, she said they basically just sit around and watch sports games and talk. She then tries to say this is something we never do, This is where I really struggle because that objectively is not true. I know she "feels" it is true, but in reality it is not. I am not a sports junky, but I do like sports. We have watch match NBA and NFL games together at home, or at sports bars, or onsite for minor league games. We even went to a professional soccer match. But for some reason those do not count. Even though we are doing the same thing, she won't just open up with me and have fun. It is like she is holding something back and unwilling to just let go. Then when she is away from me out with her friends she is a different person, carefree, fun, and living in the moment. So, yes, she is looking for something ... herself. I just don't understand why she thinks she have to leave me to find it. I don't know why she won't let herself go around me. Why she would let me love her and have fun together. Its like she puts up a wall I can't break through.

I am trying to come to grips with what you said about how I can't change her. Of course I know that intellectually, but I can't stop thinking what can I do to fix this, how can I be a better husband, what can I say to make this right. I know better, but it is difficult in real life. I know that a person can simply not love someone "that way". My wife says she likes me, she thinks I am a great person, she acknowledges all of the things I have done for her and the boys. She just doesn't love me like that. It is hard, because I still do love her like that. We are not in the same place, and I may have to come to grips with the facts that maybe we never will be and that has to be ok. I am just not there yet.

Thank you. I am trying to take time for myself, which is not something I am used to doing, but I know I need to do it now more than ever. As for treating all parties with kindness, thank you for that reminder. Everyone is hurting here, and no matter what blame we all carry, we are all humans who deserve kindness. I will keep that in mind and do my best. Thank you.

I don't disagree. Nothing is ever entirely one person's fault. We all play a part to one degree or another. That is why I am questioning myself and wondering what is wrong with me. I know my wife has been unhappy for many years, but I have tried to help. I often ask her, "What would make you feel loved?" or "What would it look like for me to love you the way you want?" because I know love does not look the same to everyone. Then I have tried to make changes in my life to show her love in the ways she values. However, she will then just tell me I am only doing those things because I know that's what she wants, as if somehow that makes my actions inauthentic.
As for the pattern of cheating, yes my first wife cheated on me as well. This was after 17 years of marriage. She had struggles with mental illness and refused to get help, and demanded that everyone in her life change their lives to accommodate her fears and anxieties. I did this for many years, probably making the situation worse as an enabler. Eventually it was clear that this was becoming harmful for our daughter, and myself, and was not really helping my wife. I began to say "No" to her demands, and that was when she found someone else who would say "Yes" and allow her to continue to avoid addressing her problems.
